skill.name: allaymc-plugin-dev
skill.description: Create, update, and troubleshoot AllayMC plugins in Java or other JVM languages using official templates, docs, and reference sources.
skill.summary: Build and maintain AllayMC plugins with guided setup, metadata, lifecycle, and Gradle workflows.
skill.author: AllayMC

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, standard LGPL license text, and documented Gradle build commands. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, unsafe network behavior, or malicious command execution in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Markdown inline code triggers command execution detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples limited to documented Gradle workflows and avoid presenting arbitrary shell snippets as automatic steps.

remediation.issue: Installation instructions reference hidden tool directories.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that paths such as .codex are installation targets only and are not locations the skill should inspect during normal use.

content.value_statement: AllayMC plugin development requires correct metadata, Gradle setup, and lifecycle code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through official references to create, update, and debug plugins.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a new AllayMC plugin from the included JavaPluginTemplate reference.
Updates Gradle project metadata, package names, authors, website, and Allay API version guidance.
Helps implement plugin lifecycle methods such as onLoad, onEnable, and onDisable.
Points the agent to Allay API, server, documentation, and AllayGradle reference folders.
Suggests local build and run commands for projects that use AllayGradle.
limitations: Requires the referenced submodules to be cloned for full documentation and source context.
Does not replace testing against a real AllayMC server environment.
Focuses on Java and JVM plugin workflows, not general Minecraft server administration.
Requires user confirmation before changing existing project structure or metadata.

use_cases.title: Start a new plugin
use_cases.description: Generate the initial project structure, package naming, metadata, and lifecycle entry class for an AllayMC plugin.

use_cases.title: Migrate an existing plugin
use_cases.description: Adapt an existing JVM plugin project to use AllayMC APIs, plugin metadata, and Gradle settings.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot build or runtime issues
use_cases.description: Use AllayMC references to inspect API usage, Gradle configuration, and lifecycle behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to create a new AllayMC plugin named ExamplePlugin with package com.example.plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Configure plugin metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to review my Gradle metadata, plugin entrance, authors, website, and target Allay API version.

prompt_templates.title: Implement lifecycle behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Add plugin startup and shutdown logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to add onLoad, onEnable, and onDisable behavior for my AllayMC plugin.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a complex plugin issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use allaymc-plugin-dev to investigate this plugin error, compare my code with Allay API references, and propose a safe fix.

output_examples.input: Create a new AllayMC plugin skeleton.
output: A short setup plan with required plugin name, package, author, website, and API version questions.
A project metadata update list for Gradle and plugin configuration.
A starter lifecycle class outline with load, enable, and disable responsibilities.

output_examples.input: My AllayMC plugin does not load on startup.
output: A checklist covering plugin entrance, package alignment, plugin metadata, and build output.
References to relevant Allay API or AllayGradle documentation paths.
A recommended verification step using the configured local server run command.

best_practices: Clone submodules before asking for deep Allay API or template guidance.
Provide plugin name, package, author, website, and target API version at the start.
Run the generated plugin locally before publishing a jar.
anti_patterns: Do not rename packages or overwrite metadata without reviewing existing project structure.
Do not assume a plugin is reloadable unless the lifecycle code supports reload safely.
Do not rely on build success alone as proof that server runtime behavior works.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps agents create, update, and troubleshoot AllayMC plugins using Java or other JVM languages.

faq.question: Does it include official references?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill points to Allay docs, Allay source, AllayGradle, and a Java plugin template when submodules are present.

faq.question: Can it build my plugin?
faq.answer: It can suggest Gradle build and run commands. The user or agent must run them in the project environment.

faq.question: Can it migrate Bukkit plugins automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide migration work, but API differences and runtime behavior still require developer review and testing.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to use?
faq.answer: The reviewed files show development guidance and documentation. The static security alerts were false positives in context.
